security_audit.summary: The reviewed skill is a Markdown workflow guide, and the static detections map to code fences, inline command examples, command aliases, and REST endpoint examples in SKILL.md. I found no prompt injection attempt, credential exfiltration intent, destructive command, or real system reconnaissance behavior. The skill does reference an external CLI, so users should review that dependency and approve commands before running them.

remediation.issue: External CLI dependency is documented without trust guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note telling users to verify the claude-flow package source and approve commands before running examples.

content.value_statement: Developers need structured collaboration when building, testing, and refactoring code. This skill guides pair programming sessions with modes, reviews, tests, and quality checks.
actual_capabilities: Describes driver, navigator, switch, TDD, review, mentor, and debug session modes.
Lists in-session commands for testing, review, navigation, Git, metrics, and role changes.
Provides configuration examples for sessions, agents, profiles, verification, testing, review, and Git settings.
Shows workflows for feature work, bug fixing, TDD, refactoring, performance tuning, and API development.
Documents session status, history, persistence, recording, background sessions, analytics, and reports.
limitations: Requires the claude-flow CLI and does not include implementation files.
Commands depend on project tools such as test frameworks, linters, formatters, and Git.
Quality checks are workflow guidance, not a substitute for developer review.
Generated code and commits still need human approval before use.

use_cases.title: Build Features With a Partner
use_cases.description: Plan implementation steps, switch roles, generate tests, and review changes during feature work.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Review Sessions
use_cases.description: Use repeatable modes, verification thresholds, and review commands for shared engineering practices.

use_cases.title: Learn Through Guided Coding
use_cases.description: Run mentor sessions that explain decisions, show alternatives, and slow the pace for learning.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Guided Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Start a mentor-style pair programming session for this repository. Explain recommendations before making changes and ask before editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Run a TDD Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me build this feature with test-driven development. Write the test plan first, then guide implementation and refactoring steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review and Refactor a Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this module for maintainability, security, and performance. Propose a refactoring plan with tests and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Full Pair Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as my pair programming partner for a complex change. Manage roles, checkpoints, tests, review, and final commit readiness.

output_examples.input: I need to add authentication and keep the code reviewed.
output: The session starts in switch mode with a senior development partner.
The plan covers authentication flow, tests, security review, and commit readiness.
The review checklist includes validation, token handling, error paths, and coverage.

output_examples.input: I have a memory leak and need a debugging session.
output: The session uses navigator mode with a debugging-focused partner.
The workflow checks runtime symptoms, searches likely sources, proposes cleanup steps, and verifies stability.
The final result includes regression tests and a concise fix summary.

output_examples.input: I want to modernize a legacy service without breaking behavior.
output: The session begins with characterization tests and a refactoring plan.
The workflow converts risky changes into small verified steps.
The final review compares complexity, test status, and remaining risks.

best_practices: Define the session goal, role, and verification expectations before changing files.
Run tests after each meaningful change and review failures before continuing.
Use review and security checks before committing sensitive or high-impact changes.
anti_patterns: Starting broad sessions without a clear goal, owner, or stopping point.
Accepting generated code without reading, testing, and reviewing it.
Using automatic commits or background sessions without clear human approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps structure AI pair programming sessions for coding, testing, review, debugging, refactoring, and learning.

faq.question: Does it write code by itself?
faq.answer: It provides workflow guidance and command patterns. The connected AI tool and user decide which files change.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need extra software?
faq.answer: The skill documentation expects the claude-flow CLI and recommends project test, lint, and formatting tools.

faq.question: Can it help with test-driven development?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents a TDD mode with test generation, implementation, refactoring, and repeated verification.

faq.question: Is human review still required?
faq.answer: Yes. Developers should review commands, generated code, tests, and commits before accepting changes.
